ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, where $AD=9$, $E$ is a point on $CD$. Connect $AE$. Triangle $ADE$ is folded along the straight line $AE$ such that point $D$ falls onto point $F$. Draw $FG\perp AD$ at $F$, with the foot being $G$. If $AG=2GD$, what is the value of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, \\
from the properties of the folding, we have $AF=AD=9$, $DE=EF$, and $\angle AED=\angle AEF$, \\
$\because$ FG$\perp$AD, \\
$\therefore$ FG$\parallel$CD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle AED=\angle AMG=\angle EMF$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle EMF=\angle AEF$, \\
$\therefore$ MF=EF=DE, \\
$\because$ AD=9, AG=2GD, \\
$\therefore$ AG=6, \\
$\therefore$ FG=$3\sqrt{5}$, \\
$\because$ $\frac{GM}{DE}=\frac{AG}{AD}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$, \\
$\therefore$ GM=$\frac{2}{3}DE$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{2}{3}DE+DE=3\sqrt{5}$, \\
$\therefore$ DE=$\boxed{\frac{9\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.

设DE=x。由图中E在CD上，即在D的正下方，所以E=(9,-x)。又因为E在折痕AE上，折叠前后的对应点D、F到折痕上的点E距离相等，所以ED=EF。于是x^2=(9-6)^2+(-x+3sqrt(5))^2，即x^2=9+(3sqrt(5)-x)^2。展开得x^2=9+45-6sqrt(5)x+x^2，所以6sqrt(5)x=54，x=9/sqrt(5)=9sqrt(5)/5。因此DE=9sqrt(5)/5。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in rectangle $ABCD$, where $AD=9$, $E$ is a point on $CD$. Connect $AE$. Triangle $ADE$ is folded along the straight line $AE$ such that point $D$ falls onto point $F$. Draw $FG\perp AD$ at $F$, with the foot being $G$. If $AG=2GD$, what is the value of $DE$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure,
from the properties of the folding, we have $AF=AD=9$, $DE=EF$, and $\angle AED=\angle AEF$,
$\because$ FG$\perp$AD,
$\therefore$ FG$\parallel$CD,
$\therefore$ $\angle AED=\angle AMG=\angle EMF$,
$\therefore$ $\angle EMF=\angle AEF$,
$\therefore$ MF=EF=DE,
$\because$ AD=9, AG=2GD,
$\therefore$ AG=6,
$\therefore$ FG=$3\sqrt{5}$,
$\because$ $\frac{GM}{DE}=\frac{AG}{AD}=\frac{6}{9}=\frac{2}{3}$,
$\therefore$ GM=$\frac{2}{3}DE$,
$\therefore$ $\frac{2}{3}DE+DE=3\sqrt{5}$,
$\therefore$ DE=$\boxed{\frac{9\sqrt{5}}{5}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure is rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is at the upper right; the upper side AD is represented by a dashed line, E is on the right side CD, and AE is the crease line. Point D is folded along AE to point F inside the rectangle and lower down. Through F, draw a line FG perpendicular to AD, intersecting AD at G and AE at point M. In the figure, FG is vertical, AD is horizontal, and CD is also vertical.

Reasoning: Given AD=9 and AG=2GD, so AD=AG+GD=3GD, giving GD=3, AG=6. Folding preserves lengths and angles, therefore AF=AD=9, EF=ED, and ∠AED=∠AEF. Because FG⊥AD, and CD⊥AD, so FG∥CD, that is, MG∥DE. Let M be the intersection point of AE and FG, then from MG∥DE and AM being collinear with AE, we can get ∠AED=∠AMG; also because A, M, E are collinear, and G, M, F are collinear, so ∠AMG=∠EMF. Therefore ∠EMF=∠AEF, triangle EMF is an isosceles triangle, and MF=EF=DE.

In right triangle AFG, AF=9, AG=6, so FG=sqrt(9^2-6^2)=sqrt(45)=3sqrt(5). Also because triangle AGM and triangle ADE are similar, so GM/DE=AG/AD=6/9=2/3, that is, GM=(2/3)DE. Since M is on FG, FG=GM+MF=(2/3)DE+DE=(5/3)DE. Thus (5/3)DE=3sqrt(5), solving gives DE=9sqrt(5)/5.
